title: What is the `void` datatype in Spark (created by `lit(None)` without a cast), why does it cause errors when writing to Parquet/Delta, and how do you fix it (`lit(None).cast("string")`)?

s1_definition.profdef: The `void` datatype (NullType) is the type Spark assigns to a literal null when no other type can be inferred, most commonly from `lit(None)` without a cast. It represents a column that is always null with no concrete type. It causes errors when writing to typed columnar formats like Parquet, ORC, and Delta because those formats require a concrete physical type for every column, and void has none. The fix is to cast the null literal to a real type, for example `F.lit(None).cast("string")`.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine adding a blank column to a National Bank report but never saying what kind of data it should hold — text, number, or date. A screen display tolerates the mystery blank, but when you try to file it into the bank's strict typed archive (Parquet or Delta), the archivist refuses because every column must declare its type. You fix it by labeling the blank column as, say, text, even though it is currently empty.
s1_definition.oneliner: void (NullType) is the untyped-null type from lit(None); typed formats reject it, so cast it to a concrete type like lit(None).cast("string").
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** The `void` datatype (NullType) is the type Spark assigns to a literal null when no other type can be inferred, most commonly from `lit(None)` without a cast. It represents a column that is always null with no concrete type. It causes errors when writing to typed columnar formats like Parquet, ORC, and Delta because those formats require a concrete physical type for every column, and void has none. The fix is to cast the null literal to a real type, for example `F.lit(None).cast("string")`.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Imagine adding a blank column to a National Bank report but never saying what kind of data it should hold — text, number, or date. A screen display tolerates the mystery blank, but when you try to file it into the bank's strict typed archive (Parquet or Delta), the archivist refuses because every column must declare its type. You fix it by labeling the blank column as, say, text, even though it is currently empty.

**One line to remember:** void (NullType) is the untyped-null type from lit(None); typed formats reject it, so cast it to a concrete type like lit(None).cast("string").

sections.s2_technical:
When you write `F.lit(None)`, Spark has no information about what type the null should be, so it infers `NullType`, displayed as `void` in the schema. This also appears when a column is derived entirely from nulls, or from a CASE expression where every branch is null. In memory and in a `show`, void is harmless — it just prints null.

The problem is at write time to a typed format. Parquet, ORC, and Delta are columnar formats that store a physical type per column (int, string, double, and so on) in their metadata. A void column has no physical type, so the writer cannot encode it and throws an error such as a message about an unsupported or null data type, or Delta rejecting a NullType column. Even creating a Delta or Parquet table whose schema contains a void column fails.

The fix is to give the null a concrete type with a cast. `F.lit(None).cast("string")` produces a string column that happens to be null, which Parquet and Delta can store as a nullable string. You choose the type that matches the column's intended meaning — `cast("double")` for an amount placeholder, `cast("date")` for a date placeholder, and so on. If a column became void through inference, you likewise cast it to the intended type before writing.

A senior nuance: this commonly surfaces when you add placeholder columns to align schemas for a union or a merge — for example adding a `middle_name` column that is null for one source — and forgetting the cast makes the downstream write fail. The habit is to always cast null literals to the target type when introducing placeholder columns, and to check `printSchema` for any `void` type before writing to a typed sink.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — The National Bank unions two account feeds; one feed lacks a `middle_name` field, so the team adds it with `lit(None)`, producing a void column. Writing the unioned result to Delta failed with a NullType error. This is exactly the void-at-write problem.

Problem 2 — The fix is to cast the placeholder null to string so Delta accepts it. This is exactly `lit(None).cast("string")`.

Problem 3 — The team wants a habit of checking the schema for void before writing. This demonstrates prevention.

What the code will do: a PySpark demo (`VoidTypeDemo`) that adds a void placeholder column, shows the write to Delta failing conceptually, then fixes it with a cast and writes successfully, for Rajesh (SAV2001) and Priya (CUR3001).

sections.s4d_java:
```python
# File: src/void_type_demo.py
# Shows the void (NullType) write error and its cast fix for the bank.
import logging
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from schema.placeholder import add_void_placeholder, add_typed_placeholder

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("VoidTypeDemo")
OUT = "data/warehouse/accounts_union"

def spark_session() -> SparkSession:
    return (SparkSession.builder.appName("VoidTypeDemo")
            .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension")
            .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog",
                    "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
            .getOrCreate())

def main() -> None:
    spark = spark_session()
    accounts = spark.createDataFrame(
        [("SAV2001", "Rajesh"), ("CUR3001", "Priya")],
        ["account_id", "first_name"])

    # BAD: lit(None) with no cast -> middle_name is 'void' (NullType)
    bad = add_void_placeholder(accounts)
    log.warning("Schema with void placeholder (will FAIL to write to Delta):")
    bad.printSchema()
    try:
        bad.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(OUT)
    except Exception as e:
        log.error("Write failed due to void/NullType column: %s", type(e).__name__)

    # GOOD: cast the null to a concrete type -> nullable string
    good = add_typed_placeholder(accounts)
    log.info("Schema with typed-null placeholder (writes successfully):")
    good.printSchema()
    good.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(OUT)
    log.info("Delta write succeeded after casting lit(None) to string")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(OUT).show()
    spark.stop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```python
# File: src/schema/placeholder.py
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, functions as F

def add_void_placeholder(df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    # lit(None) with NO cast -> inferred as void (NullType) -> unwritable to Delta
    return df.withColumn("middle_name", F.lit(None))

def add_typed_placeholder(df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
    # cast the null to a concrete type -> nullable string column
    return df.withColumn("middle_name", F.lit(None).cast("string"))
```

sections.s5_journey:
Input data: two accounts with account_id and first_name; a middle_name placeholder is needed.

Step 1: `add_void_placeholder` adds `middle_name` as `lit(None)` with no cast. Spark cannot infer a type, so it assigns NullType, shown as `void` in `printSchema`. On screen this is harmless and prints null.

Step 2: Writing this DataFrame to Delta fails, because Delta requires a concrete physical type for every column and void has none. The demo catches the error and logs that the void column caused it.

Step 3: `add_typed_placeholder` instead casts `lit(None)` to string, so `middle_name` becomes a nullable string column with a real type. `printSchema` now shows string, not void.

Step 4: Writing this DataFrame to Delta succeeds because every column has a concrete type. Reading it back shows the two accounts with a null middle_name stored as a proper nullable string.

sections.s6_takeaway:
The void datatype, which Spark calls NullType, is the type Spark assigns to a literal null when it has no other information to infer a type, and the classic way to create it is lit of None with no cast. It represents a column that is always null and has no concrete type. In memory and in a show it is completely harmless, it just prints null. The problem appears only when I try to write to a typed columnar format like Parquet, ORC, or Delta, because those formats store a physical type per column in their metadata, and a void column has no physical type, so the writer throws an error — Delta in particular rejects a NullType column outright, and even creating a table with a void column fails.

The fix is simple: give the null a concrete type with a cast. Lit of None dot cast to string produces a nullable string column that happens to be all null, which Parquet and Delta store without complaint, and I choose the type that matches the column's intended meaning — cast to double for an amount placeholder, cast to date for a date placeholder, and so on. If a column became void through inference rather than a literal, I cast it to the intended type before writing all the same.

At the National Bank of India this bit us when we unioned two account feeds where one feed lacked a middle name field. The team added that column with lit of None to align the schemas, which produced a void column, and the write to Delta failed with a NullType error. The one-line fix was to cast the null literal to string, after which the union wrote cleanly as a nullable string. The habit I adopted and recommend is to always cast null literals to the target type when introducing placeholder columns for unions or merges, and to glance at printSchema for any void type before writing to a typed sink.
